answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use time-staked activation: a new identity starts with an onyx seal that grants no voting or payout rights until it completes a long, public voyage of verifiable work spread over weeks, like a zephyr that only gathers force gradually. Each task is timestamped and cross-checked against prior behavior, so an attacker spinning up thousands of clones must pay weeks of real, sequential effort per identity instead of cloning instantly, making mass forgery slower and far more expensive than honest participation.
